statements.pressure-from-weight-of-fluid: The pressure due to the weight of a fluid at a depth $h$ below its surface is $P = h\rho g$, where $\rho$ is the density of the fluid. The bottom of a container supports the whole weight of the fluid above it, $\rho Ahg$, and dividing that weight by the area gives the pressure.
statements.hydraulic-force-ratio: In a simple hydraulic system with its two pistons at the same height, the pressure at one piston equals the pressure at the other, so $F_1/A_1 = F_2/A_2$. The force on the larger piston is larger by the ratio of the areas.
statements.gauge-pressure: Gauge pressure is the pressure relative to atmospheric pressure. Pressure gauges are built to read zero at atmospheric pressure, which is why a tire with a gaping hole in it reads zero even though there is air inside.
statements.buoyant-force: The buoyant force is the net upward force a fluid exerts on any object in it. It arises because pressure increases with depth, so the fluid pushes up on the bottom of the object harder than it pushes down on the top.
statements.archimedes-principle: The buoyant force on an object equals the weight of the fluid it displaces. If the object were taken out, the space it occupied would be filled by fluid that the surrounding fluid holds up, so the buoyant force must equal the weight of that fluid.
statements.fraction-submerged: The fraction of a floating object that lies below the surface is the ratio of its average density to the density of the fluid, $\bar{\rho}_{\text{obj}}/\rho_{\text{fl}}$, because the volume submerged equals the volume of fluid displaced and the two have the same mass.
statements.capillary-action: Capillary action is the tendency of a fluid to be raised or lowered in a narrow tube. Surface tension raises the liquid when the contact angle is less than $90^\circ$ and lowers it when the angle is greater, to a height $h = 2\gamma\cos\theta/\rho gr$.

new.name: Systolic pressure
new.statement: Systolic pressure is the maximum blood pressure in the artery, reached during each beat because of the pumping action of the heart. In a young adult it is typically about 120 mm Hg.

new.name: Diastolic pressure
new.statement: Diastolic pressure is the minimum blood pressure in the artery, reached between beats of the heart. In a young adult it is typically about 80 mm Hg.

new.name: The millimeter of mercury, $1.0\;\text{mm Hg} = 133\;\text{Pa}$
new.statement: A millimeter of mercury is the pressure that supports a column of mercury one millimeter high, which is 133 Pa. Mercury barometers and manometers are so common that atmospheric pressure and blood pressure are often quoted in this unit.

new.name: Glaucoma
new.statement: Glaucoma is the condition caused by the buildup of fluid pressure in the eye when the circulation of that fluid is blocked. The raised pressure pushes on the retina and the optic nerve and can damage them.

new.name: Micturition reflex
new.statement: The micturition reflex is the feeling of needing to urinate, triggered by the pressure in the bladder as it fills toward its normal capacity.
